screens.name: Home — default, omen unavailable and expanded policy
screens.evidence: Sheets 34–36 show normal/enlarged Home and omen states, while the supplied runtime reports contrast, navigation clearance and responsive-layout checks.

screens.name: Home — populated daily omen

screens.name: Approach — normal, enlarged, close focus and pressed action

findings: Preserve this restrained composition while making the background focus change more spatially coherent through the Home transition.

screens.name: Question — myself, populated and focused
screens.evidence: Sheets 4, 6 and 20 show populated question fields at both scales, and the runtime reports draft retention, focus restoration and field contrast checks.
findings: Reduce the visual weight of the double field outline so the plain writing area feels inset rather than framed on top of the scene.

screens.name: Question — expanded context disclosure
screens.evidence: Sheets 3–4 and 31 show expanded sent-details content preceding the question, with runtime evidence that the full disclosure remains retrievable.
findings: Group the centered disclosure into shorter labeled passages so enlarged explanatory text does not push nearly the entire question task below the first viewport.

screens.name: Question — named recipient and collapsed disclosure
screens.evidence: Sheets 4–5 show About Alex above the corresponding populated question in normal, enlarged and transition captures.
findings: Keep the recipient summary prominent while reducing the gap between disclosure and question label.

screens.name: Named person — selected, populated, corrected and empty
screens.evidence: Sheets 5–6, 21–22 and 32 show selected Someone, populated Alex and empty-name validation, with runtime evidence for constrained-form recovery.
findings: Reduce the enlarged selector/header stack so name guidance and commitment are easier to discover in the constrained viewport.

screens.name: Question and custom answer — constrained populated forms
screens.evidence: Sheets 30–32 show populated and long internally scrolled fields in constrained viewports, and the runtime reports preserved drafts and reachable labels/actions.
findings: Strengthen the internal scroll cue because partially cut text lines currently make long drafts look clipped before users discover the editor.

screens.name: Expanded editors — question and custom answer, tall and short viewports
screens.evidence: Sheets 24–25 show counters and Done/Cancel beside long drafts, supported by 24 reported browser cases with preserved content and return focus.
findings: Make the writing area's scroll boundary more explicit while preserving the visible counter and bottom actions.

screens.name: Follow-up card 1 — preparation, unselected
screens.evidence: Sheet 11 shows three preparation choices, progress and disabled Continue at normal and enlarged text.
findings: Tighten the enlarged heading-to-instruction spacing to keep the three options and continuation visually connected.

screens.name: Follow-up card 2 — obstacle, unselected and selected
screens.evidence: Sheets 12 and 14 show Time selected with an explicit radio mark and a visibly enabled Continue.
findings: Add a restrained selected-edge treatment so the chosen row reads faster without relying on the small radio mark alone.

screens.name: Follow-up card 3 — support, unselected
screens.evidence: Sheets 12–13 show three support choices and the final Reveal instruction across both scales.
findings: Keep the final-step instruction compact enough that Reveal remains visually close to the answer group at enlarged text.

screens.name: Follow-up — single/two-option, focus, pressed and selected
screens.evidence: Sheets 19–21 and 29–30 show focused Back, focused/pressed parchment and selected options, with supplied keyboard and target evidence.
findings: Strengthen parchment press feedback because the captured dimming is much less immediately legible than the selected radio state.

screens.name: Follow-up — other-input empty and populated

screens.name: Age confirmation — normal and enlarged
screens.evidence: Sheet 37 shows the direct age question, no-birthday explanation and two clearly differentiated actions.
findings: Preserve the concise wording and add a quieter local backdrop if the detailed shelf texture becomes more prominent behind the controls.

screens.name: Onboarding birthday — optional and empty
screens.evidence: Sheet 38 shows optional birthday entry, Skip and responsive day/month/year arrangement at both text scales.
findings: Visually group Skip with the optional birthday label more tightly to clarify the alternative path at a glance.

screens.name: Age blocked — onboarding and edited birthday

screens.name: Onboarding birthday correction

screens.name: Onboarding focus — optional, unselected and selected

screens.name: Birthday editing — populated

screens.name: Birthday editing — partial and invalid date

screens.name: Birth time — initial, empty and forgotten

screens.name: Birth time — invalid

screens.name: Sensitive-question redirects — planning and prediction

limitations: All scores are provisional browser judgments from the attached stills, chronological filmstrips and supplied runtime account; I did not independently run the tests or inspect a video.
Screens group their corresponding normal, enlarged, transition and named variants; related fixtures are assessed for interface presentation, not predictive quality or production wording.
A is the mean of hierarchy, typography and surfaces; F is the mean of clarity, feedback and accessibility; overall is 0.4A + 0.6F, excluding genuinely inapplicable null dimensions.
The authorized A>=9 and F>=9 threshold is not met across every screen and component, chiefly because of enlarged-content hierarchy, long centered passages and uneven scene integration.
Below-viewport content in a still is not proof of an inaccessible action; supplied scrolling and reachability checks prevent treating ordinary vertical overflow as a demonstrated hard-gate failure.
No hard-gate failure is established by this evidence; automated contrast and axe results do not establish effortless comprehension or exhaustive keyboard usability.

The room filmstrips support crossfade assessment, not continuous camera geometry, independent-layer parallax or frame-rate measurement; performance evidence comes from the separate reported browser timing run.
Physical iPhone/VoiceOver, native keyboard, tilt, haptics, actual OS sharing and native performance remain unverified, without deductions solely for that deferred boundary.
Connected Circles behavior is not demonstrated; billing and navigator.share are simulated, and the reminder screen explicitly reports unsupported browser scheduling.
Repeated novice-use evidence is absent, and the supplied live reading drive cannot establish semantic or predictive accuracy.
topFixes: Compact enlarged reveal and check-in layouts: retain centered text and full forecasts, but reduce display-type wrapping, quotation padding and distance to actions.
Improve long centered explanations and sources with clearer passage grouping, restrained publisher titles and stronger boundaries between question/source groups.
Remove the opening sequence's visible orb dim-out and align room-transition anchors to reduce the impression of superimposed paintings.
Strengthen physical integration of tall parchment, notices and the Sky panel through consistent contact, edge lighting and attachment to the room.
Make internal input scrolling and parchment pressed states more immediately visible, then capture their normal/200% before-and-after browser states.
